title: SecurityInsight -- ServiceNow test pack
note: Fictional demo data (contoso.test; every id is fake). Generated from the shipped view definitions and the engine's own functions by setup\New-SIServiceNowTestPack.ps1. Times are UTC.

cases.title: New CI
cases.what: LAPTOP-0142 is seen for the first time. It is in vImportCi with u_changed_at = this run and u_si_state = active, and, because no CMDB CI matched it, in vProposedCi too. Its Defender tag is in vImportCiKeyValue.
cases.expect: Your transform/IRE identifies it by serial_number or name + dns_domain. With creation allowed for computers, IRE creates a cmdb_ci_computer with discovery source SecurityInsight; otherwise it stays in the proposed report.

cases.title: Changed CI
cases.what: SRV-APP01 moved from tier 2 to tier 1 and gained a criticality and a data sensitivity. Its u_row_hash changed, so u_changed_at moved to this run and a delta import picks it up.
cases.expect: IRE matches the existing server (serial number) and updates u_si_tier and u_si_tier_reason. Attributes another source owns are not overwritten (SecurityInsight is the lowest-priority source).

cases.title: Unchanged CI (with a removed tag and a removed relation)
cases.what: vm-demo-app01 did not change: u_changed_at keeps its older value, so a delta import skips the CI row. Its costcenter tag and its second data disk are gone: those rows are present with u_state = removed and u_changed_at = this run. Its u_object_id is the VM id (vmId), the key Service Graph / Cloud Discovery identify a VM by.
cases.expect: No CI update. The transform removes (or flags) the costcenter key-value and the relation to the detached disk.

cases.title: New Azure resource no CMDB CI matches
cases.what: kv-demo-secrets (a Key Vault, tier 0, exposed to the internet) is new and unmatched: in vImportCi with the proposed class u_cmdb_ci_azure_key_vault, and in vProposedCi with its evidence.
cases.expect: Identified by object_id. If your instance has no class for Key Vaults, the transform maps it to your fallback class or leaves it in the report.

cases.title: Identity
cases.what: sp-demo-payroll-sync (a service principal, tier 0). Identities are handed over too, with the proposed class u_cmdb_ci_entra_service_principal and u_id_source like every other row. Whether a CMDB CI matches is unknown, so it is listed in vProposedCi.
cases.expect: Your decision: create it in an Entra identity class (identified by object_id), or ignore identities in the transform.

cases.title: No ledger id yet
cases.what: DESKTOP-DEMO9's correlation id is still provisional, so its key is its own asset id (u_id_source = asset): a provisional id moves and is never a key. vProposedCi says it must not be created from yet.
cases.expect: The transform skips creating a CI from an asset-keyed row (it may still update a CI it already matches).

cases.title: CI SecurityInsight no longer sees (in its grace period)
cases.what: LAPTOP-0077 (a client PC) was last seen 8 days ago -- its owner is on holiday. Its row stays in the hand-off with u_si_state = not-seen and its last u_last_seen; u_changed_at moved to this run because the state changed, so a delta import picks it up. It is retired only after the grace period of a client PC (30 days by default, a Pro setting per kind) unless it is seen again. Its open vulnerability stays open (held).
cases.expect: Your transform decides what not-seen means (usually nothing yet, or a flag). Nothing is retired or deleted.

cases.title: CI SecurityInsight retired after its grace period
cases.what: SRV-OLD02 (a server) was last seen 31 days ago -- past the 30-day grace period of a server -- so SecurityInsight retired it this run: u_si_state = retired, u_changed_at = this run. Its open vulnerabilities close as AssetRetired. If it is seen again it becomes active again and its findings reopen.
cases.expect: Your transform decides: a flag, a task for your CMDB team, or install_status. SecurityInsight never retires or deletes a CI in ServiceNow, and never touches records it did not send.

cases.title: Vulnerability opened
cases.what: CVE-2099-10001 on LAPTOP-0142, new this run: u_state = Open (REST: u_action = new). Its u_si_correlation_id is the CI row's key, so the CI resolves directly.
cases.expect: Your Vulnerability Response transform creates a vulnerable item linked to the CI.

cases.title: Vulnerability still reported
cases.what: CVE-2099-10002 on SRV-APP01, still reported: u_last_seen moved (REST: u_action = update).
cases.expect: The vulnerable item is updated (last_found); no second item is created.

cases.title: Vulnerability reopened
cases.what: CVE-2099-10003 on SRV-APP01 was closed by an engineer, but SecurityInsight still reports it: the row says Open (REST: u_action = update).
cases.expect: Your importer reopens the vulnerable item: SecurityInsight still sees the finding (the same rule as the SQL connector).

cases.title: Security recommendation (not a CVE)
cases.what: A Defender for Cloud recommendation on vm-demo-app01, still reported: u_finding_type = azure-recommendation, u_vulnerability = its assessment key, u_title = its name. Every security recommendation is a vulnerability, with the same lifecycle (open, update, reopen, close).
cases.expect: The transform maps a finding that is not a CVE to a third-party entry (sn_vul_third_party_entry) with u_vulnerability as its id and u_title as its name, and links the vulnerable item to the CI.

cases.title: Identity finding
cases.what: IDENTITY-SPN-001 on sp-demo-payroll-sync, new this run: u_finding_type = identity, on an identity CI (u_class_hint = identity).
cases.expect: A vulnerable item on the identity's CI (an Entra identity class), through a third-party entry -- or not imported, if your transform leaves identities out.

cases.title: Vulnerability closed: Remediated
cases.what: CVE-2099-10004 on vm-demo-app01 was absent for 3 complete runs on a machine SecurityInsight saw: Closed, u_close_reason = Remediated.
cases.expect: Closed as fixed. Remediated is the only reason that is a fix.

cases.title: Vulnerability closed: Out of scope
cases.what: CVE-2099-10005 on SRV-APP01 is still on the machine, but outside the scope this target receives: Closed, u_close_reason = Out of scope.
cases.expect: Closed with a close code that is NOT fixed.

cases.title: Vulnerability closed: Duplicate
cases.what: CVE-2099-10006 on LAPTOP-0142 had two records -- one under the asset's own id, one under its CI key. The OLDER one keeps the finding (now under the CI key); the newer one is Closed with u_close_reason = Duplicate and keeps the id it ends under. Both channels carry the close (REST: a close row).
cases.expect: Closed with a close code that is NOT fixed; the other record stays open. Coalescing on u_source_record_id keeps each item on its own record.

cases.title: Vulnerability re-keyed (one CI key)
cases.what: The kept record of CVE-2099-10006 moved from the asset's own id to the CI key (the vulnerability rows used to carry the asset id). Same record, same u_source_record_id, history kept -- not a new finding, not a close.
cases.expect: With coalesce on u_source_record_id the vulnerable item is updated in place and now resolves its CI.

cases.title: Vulnerability held (asset not seen)
cases.what: CVE-2099-10007 on LAPTOP-0077: the asset is not seen, so SecurityInsight cannot tell whether it was fixed -- the record stays Open (REST: u_action = held, the why in u_si_reason).
cases.expect: Nothing changes on the vulnerable item.

cases.title: Vulnerability closed: Asset retired
cases.what: CVE-2099-10008 on SRV-OLD02: the asset was retired after the grace period of a server, so its open vulnerabilities close with u_close_reason = AssetRetired. If the asset comes back they reopen. The close ceiling still guards a mass retirement.
cases.expect: Closed with a close code that is NOT fixed (for example "retired" / "not applicable").

cases.title: Held batch
cases.what: On 2026-10-04 Defender answered only in part: 3 of the 5 active CIs of the previous batch were missing (60%, above the connector's limit). The batch was recorded as held and never shown; the import views kept showing the complete batch of 2026-10-03.
cases.expect: Your import reads the previous complete batch again; nothing is retired by a partial collection.

cases.title: Import Set push: a complete batch
cases.what: Each output's push is one batch. Before its first row SecurityInsight writes a writing row to the staging status table (u_si_staging_status); every CI and vulnerability row carries the batch id (u_si_batch_id); after the last row it writes a complete row with the same id, the planned and accepted counts and the import sets.
cases.expect: Your importer starts when the complete row arrives and imports exactly the rows with that u_si_batch_id.

cases.title: Import Set push: a failed batch
cases.what: A call was refused part-way: the end row says failed, with u_sent_rows, u_failed_rows and u_reason. The rows that did land carry the batch id.
cases.expect: Your importer does not import the batch. Its rows come again in a later batch; the last complete batch stays what ServiceNow holds.

cases.title: Import Set push: a held batch
cases.what: SecurityInsight stopped the push before it sent anything (for example the ServiceNow check found a column missing in the staging table): writing, then held with u_si_reason; no data row was sent.
cases.expect: Nothing to import. Your importer waits for the next complete batch.

checklist: SecurityInsight is registered as a choice on cmdb_ci.discovery_source.

Every staging column is a u_ column of the view (or of the Import Set rows), unchanged. The two channels carry the same columns; every Import Set row adds the contract's envelope (u_action, u_si_batch_id, u_si_cleared, u_si_reason, u_si_replaces), and a vulnerability row adds u_row_hash and u_source_run.
Dates are UTC: a datetime in the SQL views, yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss in the Import Set rows (ServiceNow's own format, no date-format setting needed).
The transform map uses IRE with discovery source SecurityInsight; your own identification rules stay first, u_si_correlation_id (if used) is the last identifier entry.
SecurityInsight is authoritative only for the security attributes (tier, tier reason, exposure, last seen, source run); it is the lowest-priority source for everything else.
An asset-keyed row (u_id_source = asset: no ledger id yet) does not create a CI.
Proposed CIs (vProposedCi) are a report: nothing is created from them unless your rules allow creation for that class.
Key-values and relations with u_state = removed are removed or flagged, never left as present.
A CI with u_si_state = not-seen or retired is handled by your rules (a flag, a task, install_status) -- never deleted because SecurityInsight no longer sees it.
Vulnerable items coalesce on u_source_record_id when present, else on u_si_correlation_id + u_vulnerability, so a re-sent or re-keyed row never creates a second item.
A finding that is not a CVE (u_finding_type other than cve) maps to a third-party entry with u_vulnerability as its id and u_title as its name.
Only u_close_reason = Remediated closes as fixed; Out of scope, Duplicate, AssetRetired and NoLongerMonitored map to non-fix close codes.
Records SecurityInsight did not send (u_source other than SecurityInsight) are never touched by the transform.
The data source filters u_changed_at > the last import (delta), and imports only after the newest batch is complete.
A held batch changes nothing in ServiceNow.
Import Set push: the staging status table exists (default u_si_staging_status, extends Import Set Row, every column of rest/u_si_staging_status.json), and both data staging tables have u_si_batch_id.

Import Set push: your importer imports a batch only once its complete row exists in the staging status table, every complete batch once, oldest first; failed, held and writing batches are never imported.
Retention: the Import Set cleanup keeps at least the rows of the two newest complete batches of each output.

objects.title: Batches (the control row)
objects.target: Not imported into a CMDB table. Read it to know which batch the views show and why a batch was held.

columns.name: u_batch_id
columns.meaning: The batch (the SecurityInsight run) this row belongs to. Only in a hand-off database of your own.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (import diagnostics).

columns.name: u_connector
columns.meaning: The SecurityInsight connector that wrote the batch.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped.

columns.name: u_state
columns.meaning: The batch state: complete (shown by the import views), held (stopped by the mass-change guard, never shown), writing or failed.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped. Import only after the newest batch is complete.

columns.name: u_started_at
columns.meaning: When the batch was started (UTC).
columns.servicenow: Not mapped.

columns.name: u_batch_time
columns.meaning: When that batch was completed (UTC). Only in a hand-off database of your own.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (import diagnostics).

columns.name: u_ci_count
columns.meaning: How many CIs the batch holds -- the seen ones and the ones SecurityInsight no longer sees, carried with their state.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped. Compare with the rows your import read.

columns.name: u_key_value_count
columns.meaning: How many key-value rows the batch holds.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped.

columns.name: u_relation_count
columns.meaning: How many relation rows the batch holds.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped.

columns.name: u_new_cis
columns.meaning: CIs that were not in the previous batch.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped.

columns.name: u_changed_cis
columns.meaning: CIs whose content changed since the previous batch.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped.

columns.name: u_disappeared_cis
columns.meaning: Active CIs of the previous batch that this run did not see (they are carried with u_si_state, not dropped).
columns.servicenow: Not mapped. Watch u_si_state on the CI rows instead.

columns.name: u_previous_batch_id
columns.meaning: The complete batch this one was compared with.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped.

columns.name: u_reason
columns.meaning: Why: the counts of a complete batch, or why a batch was held.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped.
columns.example: 6 CI(s): 5 new, 0 changed, 0 missing against the previous batch

columns.name: u_si_batch_id
columns.meaning: The batch id (the same value as u_batch_id) -- the id every row of the batch carries in u_si_batch_id.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped. Import only rows of a complete batch.

objects.title: Configuration items
objects.target: The class in u_proposed_class, through IRE (transform map with "Use IRE", or IntegrationHub ETL), discovery source SecurityInsight.

columns.name: u_si_correlation_id
columns.meaning: SecurityInsight's stable key for the CI, kept by its identity ledger across re-imaging and id changes -- the SAME key on the CI rows and on the vulnerability rows. Treat it as an opaque string of up to 400 characters (for example mdedeviceid:..., azureresourceid:..., entraobjectid:..., or a GUID).
columns.servicenow: Coalesce key of the staging row. On the CI: u_si_correlation_id, added as the LAST identifier entry (a tie-breaker after your own rules). On a vulnerable item: how the transform finds the CI.

columns.name: u_id_source
columns.meaning: Where the key comes from: ledger (the identity ledger's id -- stable) or asset (no ledger id yet: the asset's own id, which changes once when the ledger mints one -- do not create a CI from it).
columns.servicenow: Not mapped. Use it in the transform: skip or report an asset-keyed row instead of creating a CI.

columns.name: u_class_hint
columns.meaning: What kind of thing this is: device, azure-resource or identity.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped. Use it in the transform to choose the class family.

columns.name: u_proposed_class
columns.meaning: The ServiceNow class SecurityInsight proposes (standard classes first; u_ classes are proposed extensions).
columns.servicenow: The target class of the IRE payload (sys_class_name). Your transform may override it.

columns.name: u_name
columns.meaning: The asset name.
columns.servicenow: name (IRE: Hardware rule name + dns_domain). SecurityInsight is the lowest-priority source for it.

columns.name: u_fqdn
columns.meaning: The fully qualified DNS name (lower case).
columns.servicenow: fqdn

columns.name: u_dns_domain
columns.meaning: The DNS domain, taken from the FQDN.
columns.servicenow: dns_domain (IRE: Hardware rule name + dns_domain)

columns.name: u_serial_number
columns.meaning: The serial number, where Defender, Intune or Azure report one (devices only).
columns.servicenow: serial_number (IRE: Hardware rule serial_number)

columns.name: u_mac_address
columns.meaning: A MAC address, where a source reports one (devices only).
columns.servicenow: mac_address (IRE: Hardware rule mac_address + name)

columns.name: u_object_id
columns.meaning: The cloud or directory object id: an Azure VM's VM id (vmId), another Azure resource's resource id, or the Entra object id for an identity.
columns.servicenow: object_id (IRE for cmdb_ci_vm_instance -- the vmId, as Service Graph / Cloud Discovery use it --, the cloud classes, u_cmdb_ci_azure_resource and the Entra identity classes)

columns.name: u_azure_resource_id
columns.meaning: The Azure Resource Manager id (lower case).
columns.servicenow: u_azure_resource_id (optional custom field)

columns.name: u_aad_device_id
columns.meaning: The Entra (Azure AD) device id.
columns.servicenow: u_aad_device_id (optional custom field)

columns.name: u_mde_device_id
columns.meaning: The Microsoft Defender for Endpoint device id.
columns.servicenow: u_mde_device_id (optional custom field)

columns.name: u_entra_object_id
columns.meaning: The Entra object id (identities, and devices where known).
columns.servicenow: u_entra_object_id (optional custom field); for an identity the same value is in u_object_id

columns.name: u_tier
columns.meaning: SecurityInsight's criticality tier: 0 = most critical ... 3.
columns.servicenow: u_si_tier (SecurityInsight is authoritative)

columns.name: u_tier_reason
columns.meaning: Why the asset has that tier, in plain words.
columns.servicenow: u_si_tier_reason (SecurityInsight is authoritative)
columns.example: default tier for a client device with no owner

columns.name: u_criticality
columns.meaning: The criticality SecurityInsight weighs risk with: your asset-profile rule's override, else the CMDB record.
columns.servicenow: Optional. Leave unmapped to keep your CMDB's own value, or map with SecurityInsight as a low-priority source.

columns.name: u_exposed_internet
columns.meaning: Whether SecurityInsight sees the asset exposed to the internet (1 = yes, 0 = no).
columns.servicenow: u_si_exposed_internet (SecurityInsight is authoritative)

columns.name: u_last_seen
columns.meaning: When SecurityInsight last saw the asset (UTC).
columns.servicenow: u_si_last_seen (SecurityInsight is authoritative)

columns.name: u_source_run
columns.meaning: The SecurityInsight engine run the values come from.
columns.servicenow: u_si_source_run (traceability)

columns.name: u_run_time
columns.meaning: When SecurityInsight built this row (UTC).
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (import diagnostics).

columns.name: u_discovery_source
columns.meaning: Always SecurityInsight.
columns.servicenow: discovery_source of the IRE payload. Register SecurityInsight as a choice on cmdb_ci.discovery_source first.

columns.name: u_row_hash
columns.meaning: A fingerprint of the row's content. It changes only when the content changes.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (change detection).

columns.name: u_changed_at
columns.meaning: When the row's content or its state last changed (UTC). A plain re-sighting does not move it. In an Import Set push every row is sent each run and this is the run time -- compare u_row_hash to see a change.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped. The delta filter of the data source: WHERE u_changed_at > <last import>.

columns.name: u_data_sensitivity
columns.meaning: The data sensitivity SecurityInsight weighs risk with: your asset-profile rule's override, else the CMDB record.
columns.servicenow: Optional. Map it to the field your CMDB keeps data sensitivity in, as a low-priority source, or leave it unmapped.

columns.name: u_si_state
columns.meaning: The asset's state in SecurityInsight: active (seen), not-seen (not seen for more than 8 days, still in the grace period of its kind) or retired (not seen for longer than the grace period -- 30 days by default, set per kind: client PCs, servers, service principals, users, Azure VMs, other Azure resources -- or retired early by an Admin). Seen again = active again.
columns.servicenow: Your transform decides: a flag, a task, or install_status. SecurityInsight never retires or deletes a CI in ServiceNow.

columns.name: u_si_asset_type
columns.meaning: What the asset is, in SecurityInsight's one list for every source: Workstation, Server, Mobile, Network device, IoT, Printer, Database, Storage, Web app, Key vault, Network, Container, Compute, Monitoring, AI, Integration, Backup, Security, Management, User, Guest, Service principal, Managed identity, Public IP; Other when no rule names it, Unknown when the sources say nothing.
columns.servicenow: Optional. A filter or a note -- u_proposed_class still proposes the CMDB class.

columns.name: u_si_asset_subtype
columns.meaning: The asset's kind within its type, one value: SQL Server, Domain controller, SQL Database, Storage account, Switch, ...; General when no rule names it. A CI with a SQL subtype is where SQL findings (u_si_component = SQL) belong.
columns.servicenow: Optional. Use it to pick the sub-CI (for example a SQL instance) your transform map or a script relates SQL findings to.

columns.name: u_owner
columns.meaning: The owner SecurityInsight knows for the CI (from your CMDB services). Only in a hand-off database of your own; the Pro database's views end before this column.
columns.servicenow: Optional, for example owned_by or a note. Your choice.

columns.name: u_owner_mail
columns.meaning: The owner's mail address. Only in a hand-off database of your own.
columns.servicenow: Optional. Your choice.

columns.name: u_department
columns.meaning: The department the CI belongs to in SecurityInsight. Only in a hand-off database of your own.
columns.servicenow: Optional, for example department. Your choice.

columns.name: u_batch_id
columns.meaning: The batch (the SecurityInsight run) this row belongs to. Only in a hand-off database of your own.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (import diagnostics).

columns.name: u_batch_time
columns.meaning: When that batch was completed (UTC). Only in a hand-off database of your own.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (import diagnostics).

columns.name: u_si_batch_id
columns.meaning: The batch this row belongs to. Read a row only when this batch is complete: the hand-off views show only the newest complete batch; on the Pro database and the SQL vulnerability connector, look the id up in vImportBatch (u_si_batch_id, u_state = complete).
columns.servicenow: Not mapped. Import a row only when its batch is complete.

columns.name: u_action
columns.meaning: What SecurityInsight asks for, on every row of every record: new, update (an unchanged record has the same u_row_hash), close, reopen, held (change nothing; the why is in u_si_reason) or out_of_scope (the record left the output scope; a vulnerable item closes as Out of scope, never as fixed).
columns.servicenow: Use it in the transform: create, update, close or reopen; a held row changes nothing; out_of_scope closes without a fix.

columns.name: u_si_cleared
columns.meaning: The clear marker: the columns (comma separated) whose value SecurityInsight now knows is empty. An empty column that is not listed is unknown. Never on a held row.
columns.servicenow: Transform: clear those fields; keep the value of every other empty field.

columns.meaning: What kind of thing this is: device, azure-resource or identity.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped. Use it in the transform to choose the class family.

columns.name: u_asset_name
columns.meaning: The asset name the finding is on.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (the CI is resolved from u_si_correlation_id).

columns.name: u_cmdb_ci
columns.meaning: The CMDB CI the finding is linked to, when SecurityInsight knows its sys_id (only with direct write); usually empty.
columns.servicenow: cmdb_ci when filled; otherwise the transform resolves the CI from u_si_correlation_id, which is the CI rows' key.

columns.name: u_vulnerability
columns.meaning: The finding: the id its source gives it -- a CVE id, a Defender for Cloud assessment key, a Defender security configuration id (scid-...) or a SecurityInsight rule id (IDENTITY-..., an attack path). Unique per asset; up to 100 characters (a longer id is cut and ends in ~ and a hash).
columns.servicenow: vulnerability: a CVE -> sn_vul_nvd_entry by CVE id; any other finding -> a third-party entry (sn_vul_third_party_entry) with this id and u_title as its name. Coalesce on u_source_record_id, else u_si_correlation_id + u_vulnerability.

columns.name: u_severity
columns.meaning: The severity SecurityInsight reports: Very High, Critical, High, Medium-High, Medium or Low.
columns.servicenow: Optional. Your Vulnerability Response computes its own risk; map only if wanted.

columns.name: u_state
columns.meaning: Open or Closed.
columns.servicenow: state (open / closed; closed with the close reason)

columns.name: u_first_seen
columns.meaning: When SecurityInsight first reported the finding (UTC).
columns.servicenow: first_found

columns.name: u_last_seen
columns.meaning: When SecurityInsight last reported the finding (UTC).
columns.servicenow: last_found

columns.name: u_closed_at
columns.meaning: When the record was closed (UTC); empty while open.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (closed is driven by u_state).

columns.name: u_close_reason
columns.meaning: Why the record was closed. Only Remediated is a fix; Out of scope, Duplicate, AssetRetired and NoLongerMonitored are not.
columns.servicenow: u_si_close_reason, and your close code. Never map a reason other than Remediated to Fixed.

columns.name: u_absent_runs
columns.meaning: How many complete runs in a row the finding was absent on an asset SecurityInsight saw.
columns.servicenow: u_si_absent_runs (optional)

columns.name: u_source
columns.meaning: Who opened the record: SecurityInsight. SecurityInsight only ever closes its own records; a record it never sent is never touched.
columns.servicenow: u_si_source, and the ownership check of your transform

columns.name: u_source_record_id
columns.meaning: SecurityInsight's own id of the record. It never changes for one finding on one asset -- also not when the CI key is corrected (a re-key).
columns.servicenow: The best coalesce key of the vulnerable item when present (empty for a new finding in an Import Set push).

columns.name: u_changed_at
columns.meaning: When the record last changed (UTC): opened, refreshed, closed, reopened, or an absence counted. In an Import Set push: this run.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped. The delta filter of the data source: WHERE u_changed_at > <last import>.

columns.name: u_finding_type
columns.meaning: What kind of finding it is: cve, azure-recommendation (Defender for Cloud), endpoint-recommendation (Defender security configuration), identity, attack-path, exposure or recommendation. Every security recommendation is a vulnerability.
columns.servicenow: Use it in the transform to choose the entry type: cve -> sn_vul_nvd_entry, anything else -> sn_vul_third_party_entry.

columns.name: u_title
columns.meaning: The finding's name, as its source names it (for a CVE often empty).
columns.servicenow: The third-party entry's name / short description for a finding that is not a CVE.
columns.example: Machines should have vulnerability findings resolved

columns.name: u_asset_id
columns.meaning: The SecurityInsight asset id the finding was reported on (the engine's own id; the CI key is u_si_correlation_id).
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (traceability).

columns.name: u_si_component
columns.meaning: The component the finding concerns: OS, SQL, Network, Hardware, Browser, Office, Application or Other -- one value per finding (an operating-system vulnerability on a SQL Server stays OS).
columns.servicenow: The sub-CI of the vulnerable item: a SQL finding to the SQL sub-CI (for example the cmdb_ci_db_mssql_instance under the server), an OS finding to the server itself.

columns.name: u_si_servicenow_subci
columns.meaning: The ServiceNow sub-CI the finding is linked under: OS, SQL or Other by default (component OS -> OS, SQL -> SQL, everything else -> Other); the buckets and the rules that place a finding are set per install (Settings > ServiceNow > Sub-CI mapping). One value per finding, never blank.
columns.servicenow: Link the vulnerable item under the CI's sub-CI of that name (OS findings, SQL findings, Other findings per CI).

columns.name: u_si_os_family
columns.meaning: The OS family of the asset the finding is on: Windows, Linux, macOS, iOS, Android, Network OS, Other or Unknown -- one value, never blank (Unknown when no source says which OS it runs).
columns.servicenow: Filter or route by operating system (Windows vs. Linux); not needed to link the item.

columns.name: u_si_patch_cycle
columns.meaning: Whether the finding is fixed in the monthly patch cycle: In monthly cycle (its fix was released -- or, without one dated update, it was first detected -- within SI_PatchCycle_CatchUpDays, default 30, of the collection), Catch-up (older than 1 month), No fix available or Unknown. One value, never blank.
columns.servicenow: Filter or report by patch cycle; not needed to link the item.

columns.name: u_si_batch_id
columns.meaning: The batch this row belongs to. Read a row only when this batch is complete: the hand-off views show only the newest complete batch; on the Pro database and the SQL vulnerability connector, look the id up in vImportBatch (u_si_batch_id, u_state = complete).
columns.servicenow: Not mapped. Import a row only when its batch is complete.

columns.name: u_action
columns.meaning: What SecurityInsight asks for, on every row of every record: new, update (an unchanged record has the same u_row_hash), close, reopen, held (change nothing; the why is in u_si_reason) or out_of_scope (the record left the output scope; a vulnerable item closes as Out of scope, never as fixed).
columns.servicenow: Use it in the transform: create, update, close or reopen; a held row changes nothing; out_of_scope closes without a fix.

columns.name: u_si_cleared
columns.meaning: The clear marker: the columns (comma separated) whose value SecurityInsight now knows is empty. An empty column that is not listed is unknown. Never on a held row.
columns.servicenow: Transform: clear those fields; keep the value of every other empty field.

columns.name: u_source_record_id
columns.meaning: SecurityInsight's own id of the record. It never changes for one finding on one asset -- also not when the CI key is corrected (a re-key).
columns.servicenow: The best coalesce key of the vulnerable item when present (empty for a new finding in an Import Set push).

columns.name: u_changed_at
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: When the record last changed (UTC): opened, refreshed, closed, reopened, or an absence counted. In an Import Set push: this run.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped. The delta filter of the data source: WHERE u_changed_at > <last import>.

columns.name: u_finding_type
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: What kind of finding it is: cve, azure-recommendation (Defender for Cloud), endpoint-recommendation (Defender security configuration), identity, attack-path, exposure or recommendation. Every security recommendation is a vulnerability.
columns.servicenow: Use it in the transform to choose the entry type: cve -> sn_vul_nvd_entry, anything else -> sn_vul_third_party_entry.

columns.name: u_title
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: The finding's name, as its source names it (for a CVE often empty).
columns.servicenow: The third-party entry's name / short description for a finding that is not a CVE.
columns.example: Machines should have vulnerability findings resolved

columns.name: u_asset_id
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: The SecurityInsight asset id the finding was reported on (the engine's own id; the CI key is u_si_correlation_id).
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (traceability).

columns.name: u_si_component
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: The component the finding concerns: OS, SQL, Network, Hardware, Browser, Office, Application or Other -- one value per finding (an operating-system vulnerability on a SQL Server stays OS).
columns.servicenow: The sub-CI of the vulnerable item: a SQL finding to the SQL sub-CI (for example the cmdb_ci_db_mssql_instance under the server), an OS finding to the server itself.

columns.name: u_si_servicenow_subci
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: The ServiceNow sub-CI the finding is linked under: OS, SQL or Other by default (component OS -> OS, SQL -> SQL, everything else -> Other); the buckets and the rules that place a finding are set per install (Settings > ServiceNow > Sub-CI mapping). One value per finding, never blank.
columns.servicenow: Link the vulnerable item under the CI's sub-CI of that name (OS findings, SQL findings, Other findings per CI).

columns.name: u_si_os_family
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: The OS family of the asset the finding is on: Windows, Linux, macOS, iOS, Android, Network OS, Other or Unknown -- one value, never blank (Unknown when no source says which OS it runs).
columns.servicenow: Filter or route by operating system (Windows vs. Linux); not needed to link the item.

columns.name: u_si_patch_cycle
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: Whether the finding is fixed in the monthly patch cycle: In monthly cycle (its fix was released -- or, without one dated update, it was first detected -- within SI_PatchCycle_CatchUpDays, default 30, of the collection), Catch-up (older than 1 month), No fix available or Unknown. One value, never blank.
columns.servicenow: Filter or report by patch cycle; not needed to link the item.

columns.name: u_row_hash
columns.meaning: A fingerprint of the record's content (not of the batch, the run or the action). It changes only when the content changes.
columns.servicenow: Keep it on the record (for example in u_si_row_hash) and skip a row whose hash equals it.

columns.name: u_source_run
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: The SecurityInsight run the values come from (on a held row: the run of the last values sent).
columns.servicenow: u_si_source_run (traceability)

columns.name: u_action
columns.meaning: What SecurityInsight asks for, on every row of every record: new, update (an unchanged record has the same u_row_hash), close, reopen, held (change nothing; the why is in u_si_reason) or out_of_scope (the record left the output scope; a vulnerable item closes as Out of scope, never as fixed).
columns.servicenow: Use it in the transform: create, update, close or reopen; a held row changes nothing; out_of_scope closes without a fix.

columns.name: u_si_batch_id
columns.meaning: The batch this row belongs to: <SecurityInsight run id>:<output>. The staging status table (u_si_staging_status) has a writing row and then a complete, failed or held row with the same id.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped. Import a row only when its batch has a complete row in the staging status table.

columns.name: u_si_cleared
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: The clear marker: the columns (comma separated) whose value SecurityInsight now knows is empty. An empty column that is not listed is unknown. Never on a held row.
columns.servicenow: Transform: clear those fields; keep the value of every other empty field.

columns.name: u_si_reason
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: Why the row is held or out_of_scope, in plain words. Empty otherwise.
columns.servicenow: work notes
columns.example: the output scope leaves the finding out -- closed as out of scope, not as fixed

columns.name: u_si_replaces
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: The key this record replaces (a device re-onboarded or merged). The old key gets no row of its own.
columns.servicenow: Transform: find the record by this key and move it to the row's key, instead of creating a new one.

objects.title: Staging status table (SecurityInsight staging status): when a batch is complete
objects.target: No target table: your importer reads it. Import a batch only once its complete row exists; never a failed, held or writing batch.

columns.name: u_si_batch_id
columns.meaning: The batch: <SecurityInsight run id>:<output>. The same value is on every data row of the batch (u_si_batch_id) and on both status rows of the batch.
columns.servicenow: Your importer: select the data rows of the batch by this id.

columns.name: u_si_output
columns.meaning: Which output the batch belongs to: servicenow-ci (configuration items) or servicenow-vulnerable-item (vulnerable items).
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

columns.name: u_si_state
columns.meaning: writing (the batch has started), complete (every row was accepted: import it), failed (some rows were not accepted: do not import) or held (stopped before or while sending: do not import); or feedback (information only: the import result SecurityInsight read back for a complete batch -- never a batch state).
columns.servicenow: Your importer: complete = import the batch's rows (u_si_batch_id); failed / held = do not import; writing with no end row after a few hours = the push stopped, do not import.

columns.name: u_si_connector
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: The SecurityInsight connector that sent the batch.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

columns.name: u_si_target_table
columns.meaning: The staging table the batch's data rows were sent to.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

columns.name: u_si_source_run
columns.meaning: The SecurityInsight run that sent the batch.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

columns.name: u_si_started_at
columns.meaning: When the batch started (UTC, yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss).
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

columns.name: u_si_finished_at
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: When the batch ended (UTC). Only on the end row.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

columns.name: u_si_batch_time
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: When the batch became complete (UTC). Only on a complete row -- the same meaning as u_batch_time in the SQL hand-off.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

columns.name: u_si_planned_rows
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: How many data rows the batch sends. On the writing row when it is known before sending; always on the end row.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

columns.name: u_si_sent_rows
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: How many data rows ServiceNow accepted. Only on the end row.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

columns.name: u_si_failed_rows
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: How many planned data rows were not accepted (or not sent). Only on the end row; 0 on a complete row.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

columns.name: u_si_import_set_ids
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: The import sets ServiceNow made for the batch's data rows, comma separated (for diagnosis -- select a batch's rows by u_si_batch_id). A long list ends with (+N more).
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

columns.name: u_si_reason
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: Why the batch ended as it did, in plain words.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

columns.name: u_si_version
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: The SecurityInsight version that sent the batch.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

columns.name: u_si_contract_version
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: The version of the SecurityInsight data contract the batch follows. Columns are only ever added; a rename or a removal comes with a new version.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

columns.name: u_si_mode
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: live (a normal sync), resync (an Admin asked for every record again: import it like live) or test (a test batch: never import it).
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

columns.name: u_si_new_rows
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: Rows of the batch with u_action = new. Only on the end row.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

columns.name: u_si_update_rows
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: Rows with u_action = update. Only on the end row.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

columns.name: u_si_close_rows
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: Rows with u_action = close. Only on the end row.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

columns.name: u_si_reopen_rows
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: Rows with u_action = reopen. Only on the end row.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

columns.name: u_si_held_rows
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: Records SecurityInsight holds in this batch (u_action = held, plus first-time records it does not send yet). Only on the end row.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

columns.name: u_si_out_of_scope_rows
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: Rows with u_action = out_of_scope. Only on the end row.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

columns.name: u_si_import_inserted
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: Your import's result for the batch, as SecurityInsight read it back: rows inserted. Only on a feedback row.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

columns.name: u_si_import_updated
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: Rows updated. Only on a feedback row.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

columns.name: u_si_import_ignored
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: Rows ignored, including rows your IRE onBefore script handed over and ignored. Only on a feedback row.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

columns.name: u_si_import_skipped
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: Rows skipped. Only on a feedback row.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

columns.name: u_si_import_errors
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: Rows in error. More than 0 raises a SecurityInsight issue. Only on a feedback row.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).

columns.name: u_si_import_pending
columns.required: when known (an empty value is left out)
columns.meaning: Rows not transformed yet when SecurityInsight read the result (read again at the next sync). Only on a feedback row.
columns.servicenow: Not mapped (read by your importer and for diagnosis).
